artifacts.summary: All 13 plan phases completed in one dispatch: house style sheet written, shared template helpers centralized, all 17 manual chapters brought to zero BLOCKING findings on both mechanical gates, manual recompiled clean at 131 pages.

next_steps: Task ready for postflight to mark COMPLETED. No further /implement dispatch needed.

memory_candidates.content: When bringing many Typst chapters into conformance with a bare-module-path Lean-citation gate (chapter-quality-check.sh Rule 1.2), the mechanical checker flags every literal backtick span independently, including bare filenames repeated inside a single table cell or parenthetical list. A first per-file pass that fixes the sentence-level citations often misses these in-cell repeats; always re-run the checker after the first pass rather than trusting a clean read-through, since the second pass routinely turns up 5-15% more findings than the first pass caught.

A Typst manual's own drift detector (typst-sync-check.sh Check 1, backtick-name resolution) scans literal backtick spans in ALL .typ source including // comments, not just rendered prose. Adding illustrative code examples inside a shared template.typ's comments (documenting a newly-promoted helper) can silently regress this separate checker even when the two primary acceptance gates (element-lint, chapter-quality-check) stay green, because those two are scoped to typst/chapters/*.typ only. Always re-run every mechanical checker in the extension's toolkit before declaring a whole-document sweep complete, not just the ones named in the task's acceptance criteria.
